problem: Large-load and infrastructure projects face recurring friction when comparing power availability, grid/interconnection timing, siting constraints, permitting context, and alternative energy options across candidate locations. Existing evidence supports the existence of this planning problem but does not yet prove willingness to pay for this product.
target_users: Large-load and data-center site planning teams
Utility and transmission planning support teams
Municipal or regional infrastructure planning teams
mvp_outcome: Turn user-authorized project requirements and permitted public evidence into a traceable site-comparison packet that highlights power/interconnection constraints, missing information, alternative energy pathways, and questions requiring expert review.
mvp_inputs: Candidate site list supplied by user
Required load range and target in-service date
User-supplied engineering, project, or commercial data when authorized
mvp_workflow: Normalize site names, jurisdictions, utility territories, and project requirements
Collect permitted public evidence relevant to power availability, interconnection process, transmission constraints, and infrastructure timing
Collect permitted siting, zoning, permitting, and local-policy context
Identify missing, stale, conflicting, or speculative evidence
Record alternative pathways such as storage, behind-the-meter generation, private wire, phased load, or non-firm service only when supported by user-approved assumptions and sources
Apply transparent user-defined comparison criteria rather than hidden engineering judgments
Produce a preliminary comparison matrix and ranked research queue
Generate a source-linked expert-review packet with uncertainty and escalation flags
explicit_non_capabilities: No autonomous land acquisition, contracting, supplier selection, or capital commitment
No guarantee of capacity, energization date, permit approval, project economics, or site suitability
No use of speculative queue totals as realized demand without qualification
safety_and_quality_gates: Every material factual claim must retain source provenance and retrieval date
Conflicting sources must be surfaced rather than silently resolved
Stale or non-authoritative data must be labeled
Engineering, legal, utility, permitting, and capital decisions require qualified human review
Third-party data and research use must comply with applicable access and licensing terms
High-consequence recommendations are prohibited; the product prepares evidence for review

technical_mvp.architecture: Python pipeline plus structured JSON artifacts and human-readable report output
technical_mvp.external_integrations: Optional and source-specific. No integration is assumed available until access, terms, reliability, and cost are verified.

acceptance_tests: Reject or flag records lacking provenance for material claims
Surface conflicting capacity or timing claims from different sources
Never convert queue size into realized demand without an explicit caveat
Produce identical scores from identical normalized inputs and user-defined weights
Keep engineering/legal/utility approval language out of generated conclusions
Fail closed when a required source or user input is missing
Preserve all consequential authorization fields as false
next_validation_before_build: Obtain direct evidence from at least three target users that the proposed comparison/research workflow addresses a recurring paid or costly task
Test one realistic site-comparison case using public or user-supplied data and measure preparation-time reduction and source completeness
Review data-source licensing and terms for the exact MVP sources
Perform technical/security/legal-liability review before any external release
Define pricing only after willingness-to-pay evidence is collected
claim_boundary: This specification is authorized only because Stage 3 found sufficient independent evidence to justify designing a bounded decision-support product. It is not authorization to build, sell, publish, deploy, charge, or represent the product as market validated.
